design.md's own description of WHERE the shared `.github/workflows/test.yml` staged candidate lives is self-contradictory across four locations, and the CHANGELOG.md artifact design.md's Constraint Compliance table treats as accurate (AC-022) is stale relative to design.md's own current account of Stream C's CI-step status. (1) Path contradiction: design.md's Architecture diagram (TESTYML_HC node, line 97), Protected-File Statement ('the agent stages ONE combined candidate under `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml` containing ALL FOUR streams' changes... with ONE `MANIFEST.sha256` entry', line 150-151), and Global Constraints ('all four streams' edits are staged as ONE shared human-copy batch under `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml` with ONE `MANIFEST.sha256` entry', line 544-546) -- repeated in infra-spec.md's CI/CD Sequence (line 79-81) -- all assert the staged candidate IS the file at `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml`. But design.md's own API/Contract Plan section, giving the 'byte-exact tail of the staged candidate' (line 388-390), and infra-spec.md's CI/CD Sequence two lines earlier in the SAME document (line 56-58), both cite a DIFFERENT real path: `specs/epic-136-phase3/verification/T-003/staged-workflow-candidate.draft.yml`. I confirmed against the actual repository: `find specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy -type f` returns only `MANIFEST.sha256` -- no `.github/workflows/test.yml` file exists there; the real candidate exists solely at `specs/epic-136-phase3/verification/T-003/staged-workflow-candidate.draft.yml` (624 lines, sha256 `ad07d8dfa9caa3e9119ca49030771f64ed94886742ee15fa6feeaf5611338c51`, matching `human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256`'s recorded hash). `human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256`'s own comment explains why: 'The agent cannot write that path itself: sdd-hook-guard denies every agent write whose path ends with the protected workflow suffix, and the suffix match has no human-copy carve-out.' I independently verified this empirically by invoking `plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/sdd-hook-guard.py --emit exit` with a Write `tool_input` targeting the human-copy path: the guard denies with exit 2, because `_is_protected_gate_file` (`sdd-hook-guard.py:1001-1013`) matches via `normalized.endswith(suffix.lower())` regardless of the `human-copy/` directory prefix -- there genuinely is no carve-out, so all four repeated claims about the candidate's location are factually false as written and never reconciled with the correct path design.md itself cites two sections later in the same document. (2) Stale shipped artifact: CHANGELOG.md's Stream C (#125) entry, already released under '## v1.12.0 (2026-07-28)' (CHANGELOG.md:132-134,172-174, written by commit `fd4db859`), states that CI step registration to test.yml is intentionally deferred to a follow-on feature per requirements.md Non-goals. This directly contradicts design.md's current API/Contract Plan text ('Stream C's step is part of THIS batch, not a later feature's: its Blocker was discharged before the batch was finalized', design.md line 378-380) and the actual staged candidate, which (per commit `feb3118b`) now includes the `workflow-scenarios` CI step in the same batch (verified: `staged-workflow-candidate.draft.yml:383-389`). Concrete downstream failure: a human maintainer following design.md's Protected-File Statement/Global Constraints/Architecture-diagram instructions verbatim will look for the staged candidate at `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml`, find nothing there, and have no design.md-internal signal redirecting them to `verification/T-003/`. A maintainer who instead consults CHANGELOG.md -- the release-facing historical record -- will conclude Stream C's CI-step registration is still pending in a future feature and may apply an incomplete batch or defer application of Stream C's step entirely, which is precisely the 'two sequential human-copy rounds' scenario design.md's Global Constraints explicitly says must never happen for this file. Rated Major, not Critical: the underlying deployment mechanism (SHA-256 verification of the actual draft file against MANIFEST.sha256) still functions correctly once the correct path is found, so this is an implementability/clarity gap in the design's own account of its one infrastructure-facing deliverable, not a violation of a security/regulatory constraint.
